map.string: use the natural bone direction instead of world rotation
Radius in meters of the joint markers the poser's rotation manipulator lets you pick.
Show small markers where the selectable joints are.
Whether to confirm overwriting a save file.
Leave the whole avatar (mPelvis) joint free when a BVH is saved. Off (default): the BVH locks its position and rotation (a tiny rotation is written into it); on: it is left out.
Whether to save to an external format (like BVH or ANIM) file as well when saving a pose.
Whether to stop animating with the poser when the poser window is closed.
The relative sensitivity of the poser trackpad.
Poser IK drag: feet that rest on the floor stay there while other joints are dragged.
Poser IK drag: joints stop at the range of a person (off: they may bend any way).

Serve the poser and the inventory search to AI assistants over MCP on http://127.0.0.1:PlusPoserMcpPort/mcp (loopback only, bearer token in user_settings/plus_poser_mcp.json). The token allows posing the avatar and reading the names and folders of the inventory.
TCP port (1024-65535) of the poser MCP endpoint on 127.0.0.1.
Reuse the token saved in plus_poser_mcp.json when the poser MCP server starts, so MCP clients stay registered. Off: a new token every start.

Let the MCP snapshot tool include the viewer UI (show_ui). The UI can show IMs, group chat, the inventory and other private things, and the picture goes to the MCP client (an AI service outside the viewer). Off: show_ui is refused.
Let the hair of your own avatar sway behind the head's motion. Which attachments are hair is judged from their meshes (plus/hairsway/hairdetect.cpp), not from their names. Drawn only in this viewer.
How far the hair sways (1 = default, 0 = not at all, 2 = twice as far). Scales the swing before PlusHairSwayMaxOffset softly limits it. How much it swings back is PlusHairSwayBounce.

Largest sideways / front-back offset in meters of the hair tips (30 cm or more below the jaw) while swaying (0-0.5): the sway approaches it softly instead of stopping at it. The hair above the jaw never moves.

How springy the hair is (0-1): 0 = it swings out and settles without swinging back, 0.2 = default (a lively first swing, then one small, slow swing back), 0.5 = a few swings back, 1 = keeps bouncing. Independent of PlusHairSwayStrength (how far it sways).

Find which of your attachments are hair by their shape and textures (on the head, lies on the scalp, leaves the face open, does not stand out, mostly alpha). Off: only attachments set to "sway as hair" in their context menu sway.

Judge which attachments are hair and log the score of each (search the log for "Hair sway detect"), but sway nothing. For finding PlusHairSwayDetectThreshold. Not saved: off again at the next start, so a forgotten test cannot leave the hair still.

Score an attachment needs, plus 0.25, to be taken as hair (shape: up to +3.5, textures: up to +2; research/hair-detect.md). Lower: more things sway; higher: fewer. Judgements already made stay until the attachment changes or is worn again in a new session.
Attachments set by hand in their context menu: inventory item UUID to "hair" (sway as hair) or "not" (do not sway). Overrides the automatic judgment.

Wind in the hair: 0 = off (the hair moves only with the avatar), 1 = light (default: a slight stir even when standing still), 2 = medium, 3 = strong. Follows the region's wind direction when there is wind, else a made-up breeze; gusts now and then.

Ground-truth ambient occlusion (GTAO) in place of the official SSAO: the shade in corners, under furniture and where surfaces meet. Vulkan only; needs the official ambient occlusion on (RenderDeferredSSAO), which it replaces. Costs GPU time (see PlusGtaoQuality).

GTAO and contact shadow quality: 1 low (a quarter of the pixels, 8 samples; contact shadows 8 steps), 2 medium (a quarter of the pixels, 24 samples; 16 steps), 3 high (every pixel, 24 samples; 24 steps).
How dark GTAO makes occluded places (1 = as measured, 2 = darker, 0 = none, up to 4).
How far away (m) a surface still shades another for GTAO (0.1-5). Larger: broader, softer shade.

For finding faults: how far the GTAO passes go. 0 all (normal), 1 view depth only, 2 and occlusion, 3 and the 4x4 average (the light map is not written), 4 all passes but no occlusion written (g = 1), 5 the targets made but no pass recorded.

Contact shadows: short screen-space shadows from the sun (or moon) where the shadow maps are too coarse, such as fingers, faces and feet on the ground. Vulkan only; needs sun shadows (RenderShadowDetail 1 or more). Steps follow PlusGtaoQuality.

How far (m) a contact shadow ray goes toward the light (0.02-1). Longer: longer contact shadows, more false ones. Close up a ray is kept to 8% of the screen's height, and contact shadows fade out when a face fills the screen.

Development: every 3 seconds, log what GTAO and contact shadows do at your avatar's head (its depth, how big a meter is on screen there, the contact shadow ray's length in cm and in pixels, its steps and close-up strength, the GTAO radius on screen). For close-ups.

Development: when GTAO and contact shadows are both on, write them into the light map in one pass instead of two (the same pixels, one full-screen read and write fewer; research/125 #9). Off draws them apart, for comparing.

Screen space indirect light: the colour of nearby lit surfaces (sunny ground, a red wall) comes back into the shade beside them, where the ambient occlusion darkens. Widens GTAO into a visibility bitmask; needs PlusGtao, the official SSAO (RenderDeferredSSAO) and HDR. Vulkan only.
Screen space indirect light: how much of the light near surfaces send back is added, 0 to 1 (1 = as gathered; at most 1, so the light that feeds on itself settles).
Screen space indirect light: how far (m) the light of nearby surfaces reaches, 0.5 to 5 (shortened close up, as GTAO's radius).

Screen space indirect light: how deep (m) a surface is taken to be behind what the camera sees, 0.1 to 2. Smaller lets light pass behind thin things (trunks, posts); larger keeps thick walls from letting it through.

For finding faults (screen space indirect light): 0 normal, 1 the indirect light alone over the opaque surfaces, 2 the light the samples read (the last frame, moved), 3 the same with red where it was not found, 4 every pass but nothing added to the lighting.

Development: tint the pixels marked as skin magenta (avatars' Bakes on Mesh skin and system bodies, where the skin scattering will apply) and those marked as eyes cyan (the eyes of such a face, lit with it by PlusSkinFill). While on, the main view's depth carries a stencil and the G-buffer pass writes the mark. Vulkan only; not kept between sessions.

Softer shadows on faces: on the skin only (avatars' Bakes on Mesh skin and system bodies), the ambient occlusion is weakened and the sun's shadows cast from near the skin (brows, nose, chin, hair, a hat) are filled with some of the sun's light, like a photographer's reflector. The eyes in such a face (Bakes on Mesh eyes, system eyeballs, mesh eyes rigged to the eye joints only) take 80% of the same, so they are not left dark in a lit face. Sunlit skin, clothes, hair and everything else stay as they are. 0 off, 1 weak, 2 medium, 3 strong. Part of the graphics presets (light and standard off, beautiful weak); snapshots take at least medium while the snapshot boost is on (PlusSnapshotBoost). While it is on, the main view's depth carries a stencil for the skin mark. Vulkan only.

Wet look: the ground and things look wet after rain. Base colors darker and deeper by how porous the surface is, roughness lower (more reflection), surfaces facing up most, walls a little, undersides not at all; more under a cloudy sky. Puddles on level ground with rain ripples (PlusWetPuddles). The viewer's own setting, not the region's weather; places under a roof stay dry (a depth map of the surroundings seen from above, plus/rain). While the viewer's rain wets things (PlusRainWetAll) the wetter of the two applies. 0 off, 1 weak, 2 medium, 3 strong. The graphics presets turn it off (a matter of taste: changing it afterwards keeps the preset in use). Vulkan only.
Wet look (PlusWetLook): how much of the level ground is under puddles, 0 (none) to 1 (about half of it, with the wet look strong). The puddles stay in place in the world.

Wet look (PlusWetLook) on avatars (skin, clothes and hair rigged to them, system bodies; not animesh, not unrigged attachments): 0 they stay dry (while the viewer's rain falls on them with PlusRainWetAll: a little wet from the rain), 1 a little wet (mostly glossier), 2 as wet as everything else. 0 and 1 mark avatars in the main view's stencil during the G-buffer pass.

Rain drawn by the viewer (not the region's weather): 0 off, 1 weak (a drizzle), 2 medium, 3 strong (a downpour). Streaks around the camera that lean with the wind; the drops are fixed in the world (moving the camera sweeps the near ones past), splashes on the ground near it; nothing under a roof. It also keeps the wet look (PlusWetLook) off the ground under roofs and makes its puddles ripple more; with PlusRainWetAll it wets everything it falls on. Vulkan only; needs HDR (RenderHDREnabled). Draws a depth map of the surroundings from above when the camera moves (a few ms of CPU each time).

Take the weather other people write into their parcels: a [slwx rain=.. snow=.. wind=..@.. gust=..] tag in the description of the parcel you stand in makes it rain, snow and blow here, the same for everybody who reads it (Slipstream's format). Nothing is sent. It is used only while the viewer's own rain and snow (PlusRain, PlusSnow) are both off; the parcel's wind then drives the rain and snow. Vulkan only; needs HDR (RenderHDREnabled), as the rain does.

Splash when you go into the water (and a small one when you come out), made by the viewer: 0 off, 1 small, 2 normal, 3 big. Drops thrown up, fine spray and foam spreading over the surface; the faster you come in, the bigger it is. Only your own avatar; seen only by you.

Rain and snow (PlusRain, PlusSnow): the wind's speed in m/s (0 calm, 0 to 40). The streaks lean with it, and slanted rain reaches a little way under the eaves. The snow drifts with it too, about a third as far as rain would. Not the wind in the hair (PlusHairSwayWind).
Rain and snow (PlusRain, PlusSnow): where the wind on them blows from, in degrees (0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west).
Rain (PlusRain): at most this many splashes per square meter and second on the ground near the camera (0 none). Weak rain makes 15, medium 40, strong 90 when the limit allows.

Rain (PlusRain): in a downpour the drops are large. At strong rain (3, or a parcel's weather of 30 mm/h and more) a drop is this many times as wide (1 to 4; 1: as before). Between the strong rain's start (10 mm/h) and 30 mm/h the parcel's weather grows them smoothly; weak and medium rain stay as they are. There are fewer of them, so the rain is about as thick; the splashes grow too (by its square root) and the puddles ripple more. A matter of taste; the graphics presets leave it.
Rain (PlusRain): in a downpour (PlusRainDropScale) a drop's streak is this many times as long (1 to 2.5; 1: as before).

Rain (PlusRain): water drips off the edges of roofs, hanging and then falling from the eaves (found where the overhead depth map steps by a couple of meters, so a roof against the ground or a lower roof). Heavier rain drips more. Not while it snows. Vulkan only. A few fetches of the depth map per pixel (a fraction of a millisecond) while it rains.

Rain and snow (PlusRain, PlusSnow) and your umbrella: an attachment of your avatar whose name holds one of PlusRainUmbrellaNames' words is taken for an umbrella (a dome as wide as its bounding box, with its top at the box's top). Rain and snow do not fall through it; in rain (not snow) splashes dance on top of it and drops drip off its rim. Only your own umbrella is found (other avatars' attachments have no names to look at). Vulkan only.
PlusRainUmbrella: the words, separated by commas (case ignored), one of which a worn attachment's name must hold to be an umbrella.
umbrella,parasol,brolly,傘,アンブレラ,パラソル

Snow drawn by the viewer (not the region's weather): 0 off, 1 light, 2 snow, 3 heavy. Large, slow flakes that flutter and lean with the wind; none under a roof. While it snows there is no rain (PlusRain is ignored), and snow builds up on what faces up (not under a roof) through the wet look's passes, then melts slowly after it stops (never below PlusSnowGround; none lies while PlusSnowAccumulate is off). Vulkan only; needs HDR (RenderHDREnabled). Draws a depth map of the surroundings from above when the camera moves (a few ms of CPU each time).

Whether snow lies at all: off, none lies (the snow lying is cleared at once and falling snow lays none; PlusSnowGround is kept but has no effect); on, PlusSnowGround and falling snow (PlusSnow) lay it as usual. Vulkan only.

Snow lying on the ground and on what faces up (0 none at all to 1 deep), whether or not it snows: flat surfaces first, steeper ones as it gets deeper; not under a roof, nor on avatars' bare skin (their skin bakes, system bodies, eyes: body warmth melts it). Turning it down takes the snow lying down to it at once (0 clears it). Falling snow (PlusSnow) builds up above this and slowly melts back down to it. No effect while PlusSnowAccumulate is off. Vulkan only.
Volumetric light: shafts of sun (or moon) light in the air, shaped by the sun's shadows. Vulkan only; needs sun shadows (RenderShadowDetail 1 or more). Costs GPU time (see PlusVolumetricQuality).

Volumetric light quality: 1 low (a sixteenth of the pixels, 24 samples a ray), 2 medium (a quarter of the pixels, 32 samples), 3 high (a quarter of the pixels, 64 samples). Each then blurred (depth-aware) before it is added.

How thick the air is for volumetric light (1 = standard, 0 = none; the photo tools' "Light Shaft Density" goes from 0 to 4, up to 10 here). Brighter shafts, and the light from far away dims a little more.
Samples along a ray for volumetric light (4-128); 0 uses the number of PlusVolumetricQuality. More: finer shafts, more GPU time.

Diagnostic for volumetric light, not saved: how the shafts meet alpha (which writes no depth). 3 (default): added before the above-water alpha, which blends over them by its own alpha, like the haze (no redraw). To compare only: 0 after the alpha, as first made (the light of the air behind covers leaves and hair); 1 after the alpha, with the depth of rigged alpha written after the OIT resolve; 2 as 1, and the depth of all alpha as depth of field writes it. 1 and 2 cut the shafts by an alpha threshold: nearly clear parts show as flat tinted shapes.

Depth of field behind alpha, not saved: with it on (default), the depth pass for depth of field writes an alpha surface's depth only where it is at least PlusDoFAlphaCutoff opaque, for legacy materials and PBR too (they wrote it over their whole triangles), so the background seen through a hair's clear parts is blurred. Off: as upstream, to compare.

Depth of field behind alpha, not saved: the opacity (0.01 to 1) below which alpha writes no depth for depth of field while PlusDoFAlpha is on. 0.33 as upstream's plain alpha. Higher: more of a hair's semi-clear edge shows the background blurred (and is blurred with it).

UI frames: while the world is slow and you work the UI (drag a slider, scroll bar or floater, open a menu or a combo box list, use the graphics settings), draw the UI over the last world image and redraw the world only now and then, so the UI keeps up. Chat and typing never hold the world. Preferences > Charis; environment LLRHI_UI_FRAME=0 turns it off whatever this says.
UI frames: the world counts as slow when its last frame took longer than this (ms; 50 = under 20 fps). Faster worlds are never held.
UI frames: the share of the time the world still gets while held (0.25: a world frame of 200 ms, then 600 ms of UI-only frames). 0: the world waits until you stop (or PlusUiFrameMaxPauseMs).
UI frames: the world is redrawn at least this often while held (ms), except while you drag.
UI frames: every 5 s, log the frames drawn and how long input waited for the screen ("UIFrame" lines; environment LLRHI_UI_FRAME_LOG=1 does the same). Not saved: off again at the next start.
Draw circles on the minimap around you showing how far a whisper (10 m), normal chat (20 m) and a shout (100 m) carry.
Detached windows: per floater, whether it opens in a window of its own, whether it was open there when the session ended, and the window's place (desktop pixels, monitor). Written by the viewer.
Detached windows: how many times a second a window with the keyboard in it (and the mouse elsewhere) is drawn and shown; 0 = every frame. With the mouse on it, every frame.
Detached windows: how many times a second a window nobody uses (mouse and keyboard elsewhere) is drawn and shown, for what changes by itself (new chat, inventory); 0 = as PlusDetachedMaxFps.
Detached windows: how many floaters may be in windows of their own at once (1 to 8).

Detached windows: a floater of the main window dragged by its title bar off the main window goes into a window of its own there, and the drag goes on; floaters that can go apart but whose title bar cannot be dragged get the detach button. Off: every floater that can go apart gets the detach button instead.

The retired Charis graphics preset applied last (light, standard, beautiful, official_mid), as their files wrote it. Read once, by the move to the official quality levels (PlusPresetMigrated, research/183); not written any more.
Only in the retired Charis graphics presets' copies: marks a preset file as Charis's own (they are removed at the login, research/183). Not a setting; never loaded or saved.

The move from the retired Charis graphics presets to the official quality levels is done (once, after a login; research/183): the preset that was in use went to its level (light Mid, official_mid MidHigh, standard High, beautiful Ultra), settings of the user's own were kept.

Snapshot boost: snapshots (and their preview) are drawn with every Charis enhancement at its best quality (GTAO, contact shadows, sun shafts) and full OIT, whatever the graphics preset. No setting changes; it costs time only while a snapshot is taken. Turns RenderOITSnapshotFull on and off with it. Vulkan only.

Sunbeams through clouds, all in one (the photo tools' Sky and Weather tab, the photo screen, Preferences > Charis): on puts on together the volumetric clouds, their shadows (PlusCloudShadow 0.7 or more), the sunbeams (PlusCloudShafts 1.5 or more) and the volumetric light (on, PlusVolumetricStrength 1.5 or more, PlusVolumetricQuality medium or better), writing only what is below that; off gives back each one that still holds what it wrote (PlusCloudShaftsSceneBefore). Not saved: it shows whether all of it is on, made again from those settings whenever one changes. A quality level turns it off (its values win). The quality levels, the sun's shadows and the sky are left alone.

What PlusCloudShaftsScene wrote and what each setting was before (setting name to before and wrote), to give them back when it is turned off, after a restart too. Only the recipe's own settings are read from it; one changed since it was written is left as it is.

Shadow distance: how far the sun's shadows reach and how sharp they stay there. 0 near (96 m), 1 normal (192 m), 2 far (384 m, sun shadow maps 1.5 times as fine), 3 very far (512 m, twice as fine); never past the draw distance. Snapshots take the farthest and finest while the snapshot boost is on (PlusSnapshotBoost). -1: the official shadows (for comparisons).

Glare (HDR bloom): the brightest parts of the picture (a low sun, a blown-out sky, sunlit water) spread light over what is around them, before tone mapping. 0 off, 1 weak, 2 medium, 3 strong. Part of the graphics presets (light off, standard weak, beautiful medium); snapshots take at least medium while the snapshot boost is on (PlusSnapshotBoost). Vulkan only.

Lens flare: with the sun in or near the picture, ghosts (soft discs with rainbow rims) on the line from the sun through the center, a rainbow ring and a warm halo. Fades as the sun is hidden or leaves the picture. 0 off, 1 weak, 2 medium, 3 strong. The graphics presets turn it off (a matter of taste: changing it afterwards keeps the preset in use); not part of the snapshot boost. Vulkan only.

The night sky's stars. 0 the official stars (1000 squares of one brightness); 1 the Charis star field (thousands of stars, mostly faint and a few bright, each of the colour of its temperature, a gentle twinkle that is stronger near the horizon, a few pixels wide at any field of view); 2 the star field and the Milky Way (a band of soft faint patches with a dark rift). Not drawn with an HDRI sky. The graphics presets set it (comparison 0, light and standard 1, beautiful 2); a matter of taste: changing it afterwards keeps the preset in use. Vulkan only.

Clean edges on textures with transparency (research/alpha-mask-edge-2026-10-26 (d)): when a texture used for colour (an object's diffuse or PBR base colour, the sky's sun and moon) is decoded, the colour of its transparent texels is filled from the opaque ones round them, so filtering and mipmaps do not mix a dark rim into alpha-masked and blended edges (the moon's dark fringe, a planet's black outline). The alpha is not changed. Done on the decode threads when a texture loads, nothing per frame; a change applies to the textures loaded after it. Normal and specular maps are left as they are. The graphics levels set it (off at MidHigh, the official look).
How bright the stars and the Milky Way are (PlusSkyStars 1 and 2): 1 as made, 0.25 - 4. The sky's own star brightness (the environment editor) still fades them out by day.

How bright the Milky Way is (PlusSkyStars 2), on its own: 0 hides it, 0.25 the default (2026-10-26: was 0.6, still too bright), up to 2. On top of PlusSkyStarGain, which the stars and the Milky Way share. A matter of taste: the graphics levels do not set it.

Many more faint stars (PlusSkyStars 1 and 2, research/224): about 40,000 stars of magnitude 7 - 9 added to the sky, gathered along the Milky Way's plane, so a long look at the sky shows the grain a camera records. Off by default: the sky has about a quarter of a million more vertices to draw (a fraction of a millisecond). A matter of taste: the graphics levels do not set it.

A finer Milky Way (PlusSkyStars 2 only, research/224): instead of soft patches of light, the band is baked once into a picture of the whole sky (dark dust lanes, clumps, the grain of unresolved stars; about 21 MB of video memory, a second's work on another thread when it is turned on or the sky changes). Off by default. A matter of taste: the graphics levels do not set it.

How much the stars twinkle (PlusSkyStars 1 and 2, research/176 section 11): 0 none, 0.6 gentle (the default), up to 2. The bright stars twinkle the most and the faint ones about half as much; low in the sky more than overhead, with a slight red and blue flicker near the horizon. Real time (it stops with the world freeze and holds still while a snapshot is taken). The graphics levels set it. LLRHI_STAR_TWINKLE=0 holds it off.

The real sky (PlusSkyStarsReal): how much brighter the stars of the constellations (every star on a constellation line) are drawn, so their shapes show without the lines (research/177 section 2.7): their light times 1 + 0.3 x this; 0 none, 1 the default, up to 2. Works whether or not the lines are drawn. The graphics levels set it.
PlusSkyStarsTwinkle: holds the twinkle still where it is (for photos). Not saved: the stars twinkle again at the next start.

The night sky's stars (PlusSkyStars 1 and 2, research/177): 0 the made-up star field; 1 the real stars of the Yale Bright Star Catalogue (about 9,100, to magnitude 6.5) where they stand for the place (PlusSkyStarsLat / Lon) and the time (PlusSkyStarsTimeMode). Below the horizon they are left out, near it the air dims and reddens them. The graphics presets set it (0); a matter of taste. LLRHI_REAL_STARS=0 holds it off. Vulkan only.

PlusSkyStarsReal: the latitude the real sky is seen from, degrees (north positive, -90 - 90). Default Tokyo. The photo tools' Seen From list (plus/realstars/realskyplaces.h, 49 places) writes it with PlusSkyStarsLon; a value of no place shows Custom.

PlusSkyStarsReal: the longitude the real sky is seen from, degrees (east positive, -180 - 180). Default Tokyo. Written with PlusSkyStarsLat by the photo tools' Seen From list. Not used while the sky follows SL's sun (PlusSkyStarsTimeMode 0).

PlusSkyStarsReal: the time of the real sky. 0 turned with SL's sun (the stars of the date stand where they would with the Sun where SL's sun is: the season's constellations at SL's night); 1 the real time now; 2 the time of PlusSkyStarsTime.

PlusSkyStarsReal: a time, UTC, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (the photo tools take it in the PC's time zone). With PlusSkyStarsTimeMode 2 the sky of that time; with 0 its date (the Sun's place among the stars). Empty: now (today).

PlusSkyStarsReal: the constellation lines, faint, between the stars (d3-celestial's lines, research/177 section 2.6), on any sky that shows the stars, dimmed with them by its star brightness (not by the sun). The graphics presets set it (0); a matter of taste.
PlusSkyStarsLines: how bright the lines are, 0 - 1 (0.35 about as a faint star).
PlusSkyStarsLines: how wide the lines are, pixels (0.5 - 3).

PlusSkyStarsReal: the constellation pictures (Stellarium's modern sky culture, Free Art License), faint and bluish over the real sky, on any sky that shows the stars, dimmed with them by its star brightness (research/288). Apart from PlusSkyStarsLines. A matter of taste, off by default.
PlusSkyStarsArt: how bright the pictures are, 0 - 1 (0.5: their brightest about as a fifth-magnitude star).

Volumetric clouds (research/186, research/244): the main view's clouds are a layer with a thickness at the world altitude [the sky's max_y, max_y + PlusCloudThickness * max_y], marched along each pixel's view ray, so that clouds have a height and a top brighter than their base (the base lit as the 2D clouds are; they come nearer when the camera flies up). They stand where the 2D clouds are, around the camera, and let through what the 2D clouds do: the same sky has the same cover either way. Their colours are the 2D clouds' own. Off draws the 2D clouds as official. Reflections, mirrors and probes keep the 2D clouds; a camera above the layer sees none. Off at every quality level for now (switch it on by hand). Vulkan only.

The thickness of the volumetric clouds' layer, as a share of the sky's max_y (the layer's base altitude): 0.2 is about 320 m under the default 1605 m. The thickest part of a cloud reaches the top; thin clouds stay low. It changes their height, not how much of the sky they hide. Only with PlusVolumetricClouds.

The shading of the volumetric clouds (0 to 2): each place is lit as the 2D clouds light it (their colours and self shadow), with the sun's share raised towards a cloud's top by this much (1: 2D's share at the base, 1.5 times it at the top; the ambient light and the haze as 2D's). 0: the 2D clouds' light. Never brighter than the 2D clouds' sun and ambient light together. Only with PlusVolumetricClouds.

Billows on the volumetric clouds' tops (0 to 1.5): how much a fine pattern raises and lowers each cloud's top, as a share of its height (0.6: about a quarter up or down). Only low in the sky, where the clouds are seen from the side (below about 12 to 27 degrees of elevation): seen from below, lumps on the tops look mottled (research/244 fix4). 0: smooth domes, and one texture read less per step. It does not change how much of the sky the clouds hide. Only with PlusVolumetricClouds.

How much of the 2D clouds' fine pattern shapes the volumetric clouds' tops (0 to 1): 0 the large shape alone (round tops; the fine pattern still shows in how much each place lets through, as in 2D), 1 all of it (a sky of small round lumps, mottled). Only with PlusVolumetricClouds.
Steps of each pixel's march through the volumetric clouds' layer (8 to 32): more is smoother and costs more GPU time. Only with PlusVolumetricClouds.

The shadow of the volumetric clouds on the ground (and on what the sun light pass lights): how much of the sun the clouds above a place take out where they are thickest, 0 to 1 (0: none, no map is made). A map of how much of the sun the clouds above each place take out is made around the camera and the sun light pass reads it where the way to the sun crosses the layer. Translucent surfaces and water are not shaded by it. Only with PlusVolumetricClouds.

How far from the camera (m, 2000 to 12000) the volumetric clouds' shadow map reaches: the map is 256 by 256, so a larger radius is coarser. Past it the clouds cast no shadow. Only with PlusVolumetricClouds and PlusCloudShadow.

Sunbeams through the volumetric clouds (research/253), 0 to 4 (0: off, the default). The light shafts' march reads the clouds' shadow map: the light reaching its air is dimmed by the clouds above it, and past it, up to the clouds' base or the scene, the sky's own haze is laid out along the clouds' shadow, brighter where the map is clearer than around the camera, darker where it is darker. The far air is as thick as the sky's haze times this. Only with PlusVolumetric, PlusVolumetricClouds and PlusCloudShadow, the sun's shadows, the volumetric clouds drawn (not under an HDRI sky, below their layer) and the light above about 7 degrees; the far air only with PlusVolumetricAlpha 3. Not in the graphics presets. Vulkan only.

The night clouds under a classic (WindLight) sky with RenderSkyAutoAdjustLegacy on: the tone mapping's curve crushes their dark grey to black. 0 as official; 1 shows them as the same sky does without the auto-adjust (a grey a little above the sky); in between, part way. Only the clouds change, only at night (from about 1 degree of the sun below the horizon, full from 8); not under HDR (EEP) skies or with the auto-adjust off. The graphics presets set it (comparison 0, the others 0.75); a matter of taste. Vulkan only.

The rainbow in the sky. 0: off, as official (the sky's own rainbow texture, set by its moisture level). 1: by hand: the rainbow of PlusRainbowKind, always, worked out from the light (the sun, or by night the moon) and the drops (its colours, the secondary bow, the supernumeraries, the fogbow), in place of the official one. It is in front of the clouds and in the water's reflection; not on an HDRI sky. None while neither the sun nor the moon is up. A matter of taste: the graphics presets leave it. Vulkan only.

Which rainbow PlusRainbow 1 shows: 0 the primary alone; 1 with the secondary (its colours the other way round, a dark band between); 2 with supernumeraries (small even drops: pink and green bands inside); 3 fogbow (fog's droplets: broad and white); 4 sunset (red); 5 moonbow (pale); 6 twinned (two bows from one foot).

How bright the rainbow of PlusRainbow is, 0 to 1: its brightest point is this times half its light (the sunlight or the moonlight the sky's haze takes there). Not changed by the exposure: the rainbow is in the sky's own light.

Cross filter (star filter): rays of light from bright small lights (lamps, car lights, the sun, glints on water), in the light's own color, as a star filter on a camera lens draws them. Lit walls and the sky get none, the stars only a faint short cross (PlusCrossFilterSky). The rays' length is a share of the picture's height (at most about 4.5%, 7.5% and 12% of it each way), so a large snapshot looks as the screen does. 0 off, 1 weak (only the very brightest lights have rays), 2 medium, 3 strong (weaker lights have them too). The graphics presets turn it off (a matter of taste: changing it afterwards keeps the preset in use); not part of the snapshot boost. Vulkan only.
Cross filter: how many rays each light has: 4 (a cross), 6 or 8 (PlusCrossFilter).
Cross filter: the rays turned by this many degrees (0: one ray points straight to the right; PlusCrossFilter).

Cross filter: the rays of points of the sky (the stars) times this, 0 (none) to 1 (as long and bright as a lamp's). The sun's rays (the moon's at night) are not weakened. Default 0.05: a faint short cross at most (PlusCrossFilter).

Development: the glare, lens flare and cross filter are added in the tone mapping pass instead of a pass of their own (one full-screen read and write fewer; research/125 #7). The same sums, but not rounded to half floats in between, so a few pixels may differ by 1/255. Off: their own pass, as before.

Shadow detail: how thin a sun shadow (legs, railings, hair) stays at a distance. 0 normal, 1 fine (sun shadow maps 1.5 times as fine), 2 very fine (twice as fine). The bias becomes a length along the light per cascade (a few texels plus what the sun's height needs, never more than the official one). Snapshots take the finest while the snapshot boost is on (PlusSnapshotBoost). -1: the official bias and blur (for comparisons).

Shadow focus: 1 fits the sun shadow cascades to the subject (the camera's focus: your avatar, or what the camera was pointed at), so the cascade holding it and its shadow ends right past them and its texels are as fine as they can be there; 0 spreads them from the camera (the shadow distance's split exponent). Snapshots always fit to the subject. Things far nearer or farther than the subject get coarser shadows. -1: official.

Development: every 3 seconds, log where your avatar is in the sun shadow cascades (its depth, the cascade, its texel and bias, how far the shadow starts from the feet, the screen-space blur there). For comparing what is seen with the numbers. Not saved: off again at the next start.

With the shadow detail on (PlusShadowPrecision 0 or more, Vulkan): the casters of the sun's shadows get a slope-scaled depth bias, so the ground the sun grazes needs no long bias of its own and a shadow starts right at the feet (about a texel away instead of 30 to 90 cm with a low sun). Off: the receivers' bias covers the ground's slope, as before (for comparisons).

The sun shadows' receivers are moved along their normal (1.5 texels of the cascade where the light grazes them, at most 10 cm) before the shadow map is read, so curved surfaces the light grazes (the side of a nose, cheeks) do not shadow themselves in bands. Off: for comparisons.

Stable sun shadow cascades: orthographic, their texel grid fixed in the world (center on whole texels, size in 9% steps, turning with the camera only in 22.5-degree steps), so fine shadows such as leaves do not shimmer as the camera moves. Costs some sharpness (up to about 1.2x coarser texels, the official perspective cascades' extra detail near the eye). Off: the official cascades (for comparisons).

With stable sun shadow cascades: the shadow grid does not turn with the camera and its size changes only on a coarser ladder, so a thin gap's light (a fence's slits) does not come and go with the camera position. Costs sharpness (the grid is sized from the receivers' box diagonal on both axes: texels coarser than the camera-fitted grid, by sun height (simulated, not measured): at 60 degrees 1.0-1.3x across and 1.8-5.2x in depth, at 15 degrees 1.4-2.2x and 1.1-6.2x, at 85 degrees 1.0-1.3x and 1.8-4.4x; raise the shadow detail to make up). Turning the camera mostly leaves the grid; it is not guaranteed never to step. Off: the grid turns in 22.5-degree steps and follows the receivers in 9% steps.

While the sun or moon moves with the day cycle, the direction the sun shadows are made with is held and follows the live one only when it is this many degrees away. With stable cascades (PlusShadowStabilize) the texel grid turns with the light, so a drifting light made the shadows shimmer; held, the shadows stay still and move a little at a time. Larger: calmer but coarser steps. 0: the live direction every frame.

Moving sun shadows (research/151): while the camera moves, a stable cascade's cached static shadows are moved by whole texels and only the strips that came into view are drawn, instead of drawing every static caster again each frame. The shadows look the same as drawn whole (PlusShadowShiftVerify checks it). Needs stable cascades (PlusShadowStabilize). Also keeps each cascade's depth range in steps (as PlusShadowZRound). Fast turns, the sun moving and a 2 s refresh still draw them whole. While on, the dither of half transparent casters follows the cascade's texel grid (moves are an even number of texels across), so moved and whole shadows dither alike. Off: drawn whole whenever the camera leaves the cached cascade. With LLRHI_CUE_DIR, shadowshift.toggle flips it without saving (A/B).

For PlusShadowShift (research/158 S4): while the camera moves, a group the sun shadows see for the first time that was built more than 3 seconds ago counts as settled at once, so it goes into the cached shadows (drawn once) instead of being drawn with the moving casters every frame for a few seconds. Only which layer draws it changes: the shadows look the same. No effect while PlusShadowShift is off.

For PlusShadowShift (research/158 S4): when the static casters where the moved and the cached cascade overlap differ from what the cached shadows hold (a group gone, changed or come, as while loading), only the rects of those casters are cleared and drawn again instead of the whole cascade. The shadows look the same as drawn whole (PlusShadowShiftVerify checks it). No effect while PlusShadowShift is off.

Development check for PlusShadowShift (heavy, not saved): one moved cascade a frame is also drawn whole with the same projection, and at the next frame both are read back and compared; the log (RHIShadow) says how many texels differ ("shift verify cascade k: N of M texels differ"). Expected: none, or a few at the old window's edge by one depth step.

Development switch for PlusShadowShift (not saved): a moved cascade draws all its static casters over the moved depth instead of the strips that came into view only. Slower than off; tests the move's copies alone (with PlusShadowShiftVerify).

Development switch (not saved): each stable sun cascade's depth range is kept in steps (whole steps of at least 1/8 of the receivers' depth, a step to spare at each end), as PlusShadowShift does, without the move. For comparing pictures with it off: with the shadow detail on (PlusShadowPrecision not -1) the shadows should look the same. No effect with the official detail.

Sun shadows (research/178 C2): small moving objects far from the camera (scripted, rotating or physical objects whose bounding radius is at most PlusShadowSkipFarSmallRadius, beyond PlusShadowSkipFarSmallDistance) cast no shadow, which saves drawing them into every shadow cascade each frame. Avatars, their attachments and animated objects always keep their shadows; still objects are not affected. Not for snapshots or reflection probes. Off: the official shadows.

For PlusShadowSkipFarSmall: how far from the camera (metres, to the object's nearest point) a small moving object must be to lose its shadow (8 to 1024). 48 m is about the middle of the third sun shadow cascade at the standard shadow distance.
For PlusShadowSkipFarSmall: the largest bounding radius (metres, the whole linkset) of a moving object that loses its shadow when far (0 to 4; 0: none).

Shadow penumbra (research/187): how many times the penumbra the sun's disc makes (about 0.53 degrees, 1 is the physical one), so a sun shadow is sharp where it starts at its caster's foot and softer the farther it falls (a tree's top, a railing's shadow across the floor). 0 off (the official read). Reads the two nearest sun cascades of the main view with a few more taps; needs the sun shadows and PlusShadowStabilize. Translucent surfaces, water, probes and mirrors keep the official shadows. Snapshots use more taps. Vulkan only.

Shadow softness: how soft the edges of the sun's shadows are. 0 sharp, 1 slightly sharp (the default: far shadows keep their thin parts), 2 normal, 3 slightly soft, 4 soft. Sets the screen-space blur of the shadows (the shadow's Gaussian, RenderShadowBlurSize) and holds it to a length in meters (3, 6, 12, 20, 30 cm each way) so far shadows are not smeared away. Kept in snapshots (a choice of look). Written by the Charis presets but not part of "preset in use". -1: the official blur (for comparisons).

Look: the color grading LUT applied to the finished image (before the HUD and the UI), for the screen and snapshots alike. Empty: none (the pass is not drawn). A shipped look's folder name in app_settings/plus/looks, or "user:" and a folder or .cube/.png file name in the look folder of the user's data folder. The graphics presets set none (a matter of taste: changing it afterwards keeps the preset in use). Vulkan only.
How strongly the look is applied, 0 to 100 % (mixed with the image as it was; scales the look's own strength).
Apply the look to snapshots only (their preview too); the screen keeps its own colors.
Photo tools: the looks the user starred, in their order (an array of PlusLook values). Shared by every account.
Photo tools: the last ten looks put on from the tool, newest first (an array of PlusLook values). Shared by every account.
Painted style applied to the finished image before the look and the effects (research/142): cartoon, watercolor, sketch or oil. Empty: none. Vulkan only.
How much of the painted style is mixed in, 0 to 100 % (0: the image as it was).
Apply the painted style to snapshots only (their preview too); the screen stays as it is.

Ocean (retired 2026-10-31, off): white edges where the water is shallow, and waves that come in toward the shore on the sea (open water; ponds get only a thin edge). Shown on the water seen from above. No longer in the photo tools or the quality levels, and not kept between starts: an older value in settings.xml goes back to off at the next start, and presets do not set it. Debug Settings can still turn it on for one session.

Development: the water shader skips the shore foam where it would be exactly nothing (30 m or more from the shore, or neither sea nor pond); the same pixels, less work on open water (research/125 #20). Off computes it everywhere, for comparing.
Development: no shore field is made for a square with no water in it (it would draw no foam anywhere; the same pixels, a shorter pause; research/125 #12). Off makes it anyway, for comparing.

Ocean: the smallest body of water (square meters) that counts as sea and gets waves. A quarter of it is enough where the water goes on past the loaded terrain. Smaller water is a pond: a thin edge only. Takes effect when the shore field is next made.

Where the depth of field focuses (needs RenderDepthOfField): 0 = as the official viewer does, 1 = the point under the mouse cursor (while it is over the world view), 2 = your own avatar, 3 = the avatar of PlusFocusAvatar, 4 = a place clicked on (choosing it starts the picking: a left click on the world puts the focus there and reaches no object, until Esc or another mode; the place is not saved, so a session that would start in 4 starts in 0). The focus follows the target when it or the camera moves; when the target cannot be seen the official focus is used.
The part of the avatar the focus lock aims at (PlusFocusMode 2 and 3): 0 = the eyes (between them), 1 = the chest, 2 = the whole body (the pelvis).
The avatar the focus lock follows in PlusFocusMode 3: its id (a UUID). Empty: none chosen.

Depth of field focuses through glass (needs RenderDepthOfField): with it on (default), a see-through surface of the world (less than 90% opaque: a window pane, a glass wall) takes no focus. The depth of field blurs what is seen through it by its own distance (a face behind glass stays sharp when focused on), and the cursor focus (PlusFocusMode 1) goes on through it to what is behind. Avatars and their attachments keep their depth. Off: the glass holds the focus, as the official viewer does.

Camera gaze: 0 = off, 1 = only your own avatar looks at the camera, 2 = every drawn avatar does (only while PlusGazeAllowEveryone is on, else counts as 1). The eyes turn first, the head only for what the eyes cannot reach. Overrides animations and the AO; drawn only in this viewer (and in snapshots), nothing is sent to others.

How far the eyes may turn from where the head points, in degrees (0-60), for camera gaze. The official limit is about 27. Large values show too much white of the eye; 0 makes the head do all the turning (for mesh heads whose eyes do not move).
The most the head (neck and head together) may turn for camera gaze, in degrees (0-60), for what is beyond the eyes' reach. The torso never turns. 0 = eyes only.

How far the eyes may turn up or down from where the head points, in degrees (0-40), for camera gaze. Small, because looking up or down shows the white of the eye (mesh eyes may need less). What the eyes cannot reach goes to the head (PlusGazeHeadPitchMax). Sideways: PlusGazeEyeLimit.
The most the head may nod up or down for camera gaze, in degrees (0-60), for what is beyond the eyes' up-down reach. Sideways: PlusGazeHeadMax.

Diagnostics only (off by default). Camera gaze diagnostics: while PlusGazeMode is on, write one line every 3 seconds to the log (channel Gaze) with your avatar's target angles, what went to the head and eyes, and the angle between the eye bones and the camera. Not kept between starts.

How much the eyes cross for a near camera in camera gaze (0-1): 1 = each eye aims at the camera from its own place (geometrically exact), 0 = both eyes parallel (as if the camera were far). Between: a mix. Lower it if one eye seems to look outward.

Turns the avatar's left eye sideways by this many degrees (-20 to 20) in camera gaze; positive turns it toward the avatar's left (outward for the left eye). To correct a mesh eye whose pupil does not sit on the bone's forward axis. Default 0.

Turns the avatar's right eye sideways by this many degrees (-20 to 20) in camera gaze; positive turns it toward the avatar's left (inward for the right eye). To correct a mesh eye whose pupil does not sit on the bone's forward axis. Default 0.

Camera gaze reaches as far as the picture is wide: the head's sideways limit is raised (never lowered) so that someone standing straight at the edge of the picture still looks at the lens: half the horizontal field of view plus 5 degrees, minus the eyes' own limit, up to PlusGazeHeadMaxAbs. Up/down likewise (half as much). Off: only PlusGazeHeadMax and PlusGazeHeadPitchMax.

The most the head may turn sideways for camera gaze when PlusGazeFovAdaptive raises the limit, in degrees (0-60). Keeps the head of someone at the edge from turning too far; up and down it is half of this.

Allow the camera gaze mode "everyone" (PlusGazeMode 2: all drawn avatars look at the camera). Off by default in public builds, where mode 2 counts as 1 (your own avatar only): changing how other people appear to you may fall under the third-party viewer policy 2.k. For the author's own testing only, so it is kept out of Debug Settings and Quick Preferences (HideFromEditor) and never saved (Persist 0): to test, write it with 1 in the user's settings.xml before a start; it holds for that session only.
Share of the head turn taken by the neck joint (0-1), the rest by the head joint, for camera gaze. Keeps the neck from twisting too much.
How slowly camera gaze follows a moving camera, in seconds (0 = instantly, 0.15 = default).

Photo tools (Charis > Photo Tools): the photo preset last chosen (portrait, backlight, sunset, night, studio, natural, autumn), empty for none. Only a label: the values it set are the viewer's own settings (RenderExposure, CameraFNumber, PlusGlare, ...).
Photo tools: the named camera positions (an array of maps: name, region, position and focus point in global coordinates, field of view). Shared by every account.
Photo tools: the single temporary camera position (Save Here / Back to It). Empty: none saved.
Photo tools: going back to a saved camera position glides there (true) instead of jumping (false).

World freeze: stops the world's time (avatar animations, moving objects, particles, texture animations, flexi prims, clouds, waves) while the camera, the UI and every setting keep working. The simulator's movement updates are kept (the latest per object) and applied when the world runs again. Not saved: the viewer always starts with the world running. The photo tools' button sets this; plus::freeze::setFrozen() does the same.

While the world is frozen, the looks of the objects already shown stay too: the simulator's full updates (color, alpha, full bright, glow, point light, textures, shape; what a script such as a lightning flash changes) are kept, the latest per object, and applied when the world runs again. New objects, avatars, attachments, selected objects and links always go through. Off: only the movement is held, as before.
After this many seconds frozen, the held updates are dropped and the objects are asked for again from the simulator when the world resumes.

The most objects whose updates (movement, and looks with PlusWorldFreezeAppearance) are held while frozen; past this the held data is dropped and the objects are asked for again when the world resumes.
Use the viewer side Animation Overrider (Firestorm: UseAO).

After login, when the AO has no set and Firestorm's #AO folder has some, ask whether to copy them (plus/ao). The question's "Do not ask again" turns this off; the AO window's Get from Firestorm button works either way.
Let the Animation Overrider replace standing and turning while it is on (Firestorm: UseAOStands). Switched on with the AO.
The Animation Overrider's set and animation per state at the last logout (Firestorm: FSCurrentAOState).
Show the full Animation Overrider window (true) or the small one (false) (Firestorm: UseFullAOInterface).
Size of the full Animation Overrider window while the small one is shown (Firestorm: floater_rect_animation_overrider_full).
Diagnostics only (off by default). Log how long each Animation Overrider change takes in the viewer and until the inventory server has answered (log tag PlusAO). Not kept between starts.
Fine turn: the angle in degrees of one step (Ctrl+Left/Right, or the turn buttons of the Move floater). Everyone sees the new facing.
Photo tools: the settings the user starred, shown on the Home tab (an array of item names: a setting's name, or param:brightness and so on). Shared by every account.
Photo tools: the user's own presets (an array of maps: name, values = setting name to value). Shared by every account.
Photo tools: the size of the one-press snapshot, the long side: 0 the window as it is, 1 2K (1920), 2 4K (3840), 3 6K (5760), 4 8K (7680).
Photo screen: the mode it opens in, and the last one used: false the detailed mode (the world is the shape of the photo, the panels are around it), true the simple mode (the world fills the window).
Photo screen (detailed mode): draw the focus frame (four corners and a cross, with who is sharp and how far) on the target of the focus lock.
Photo tools: the shape of the one-press snapshot: 0 as the window, 1 16:9, 2 3:2, 3 4:3, 4 1:1, 5 9:16 (portrait), 6 2:3 (portrait).

Photo tools: how much GPU memory a pixel of a one-press snapshot takes (bytes): the screen targets, the shadow maps and the transparency buffers of the picture, on top of what is in use (about 2.6 GB for 4K, research/109). Sizes that do not fit in the driver budget are switched off in the size menu. Raise it if the GPU stops on big pictures.
The Quick Preferences window shows its editor for the list of settings (Firestorm: QuickPrefsEditMode).
The setting selected in the Quick Preferences editor; the editor's widgets are enabled while this is not empty (Firestorm: QuickPrefsSelectedControl).

Fine move: the distance in centimeters one step should carry the avatar (Ctrl+Shift+arrows, or the arrow buttons of the Move floater). The simulator moves the avatar by a fixed amount for each nudge, so this is rounded to whole nudges, and never less than one (PlusNudgeUnitCm).
Learned by the viewer: centimeters one nudge carries the avatar (measured after each fine move made from standing still).
Show the message "the world view is held while you use the UI" while the UI frames hold the world picture (plus/uiframe). Off by default.
Receive group chat only from the groups set to "Always receive" (allowlist) in the group window; the chat of every other group is refused (plus/groupwhitelist).
Camera shot: how much the move is (2: twice as close, or twice the zoom).
Camera shot: how long the move takes (seconds).
Camera shot: how the move starts and stops (0 even, 1 smooth, 2 slow start, 3 slow stop).
Camera shot: the part of the avatar locked on (0 face, 1 chest, 2 whole body).
Camera shot: how far round the subject an orbit goes (degrees, 360 is once round).

Camera roll (tilting the camera): degrees, 0 level, positive tilts the camera to the right (the horizon turns counter-clockwise), negative to the left. Not saved between sessions; the reset of the camera (Esc, reset view, a camera preset) sets it to 0. Ignored while the flycam (3D mouse) drives the camera. Set by the photo tools.

3D mouse (flycam): while this button is held, pushing or pulling the cap changes the field of view (zoom) instead of moving the camera. Button number from 0 (0 is the flycam on/off button, 1 is the right button of a SpaceMouse Compact); -1 turns it off. Not used when the zoom axis (JoystickAxis6) is assigned, or with ZoomDirect.

3D mouse (flycam): how fast the field of view changes while the zoom button is held (multiplies the push/pull axis after its own dead zone; the zoom axis settings FlycamAxisScale6 and FlycamAxisDeadZone6 are not used). Negative reverses the direction.
Camera roll: how fast the keys (roll_left / roll_right, R and T by default) tilt the camera while held, in degrees a second; three times as fast with Shift (plus/photomode/photokeys.cpp).

Photo tools: the old marker of PlusPhotoKeysCommands (1 = the first five commands were done). Read while PlusPhotoKeysCommands is empty; set to 0 when that list is written (plus/photomode/photokeys.cpp).

Photo tools: the key commands whose default keys were put into the user's own key_bindings.xml, separated by spaces (each once; a command of the flycam's mode as flycam:name; plus/photomode/photokeys.cpp). Empty it to have the missing ones added again the next time the viewer starts.

Photo tools: ignore the plane the region sends to keep the camera out of walls and objects (the CameraConstraint message), so the camera can be put behind them. Works only in the photo mode (while the photo screen is on or the photo tools window is open and not minimized); out of it the region's plane stands even with this on. The other limits of the camera stay (DisableCameraConstraints lifts those).

Photo tools: the favorite skies that are items of the library (their ids are the same in every account, so every account sees them). An array of maps: item, asset, name, water, library. The other favorite skies are in each account's own settings (PlusPhotoSkyFavorites); the waters have lists of their own (PlusPhotoWater*).
Photo tools, Sky & Weather tab: the list of skies (the tabs All / Favorites / Recent, the search, the tree) is open (true) or folded away (false), so the sections under it have room.
Photo tools, Sky & Weather tab: the list of waters (the tabs All / Favorites / Recent, the search, the tree) is open (true) or folded away (false), so the sections under it have room.

Photo tools: the favorite waters that are items of the library (their ids are the same in every account, so every account sees them). An array of maps: item, asset, name, water, library. The other favorite waters are in each account's own settings (PlusPhotoWaterFavorites).
Photo tools: the composition guide is shown over the screen (never in a picture).
Photo tools: the guide: 0 none (only the frame of the photo), 1 thirds, 2 golden ratio, 3 center cross, 4 diagonals, 5 grid 4x4, 6 grid 6x6, 7 horizon (follows the camera tilt).
Photo tools: the color of the guide lines: 0 white, 1 black, 2 yellow, 3 red.
Photo tools: how strong the guide lines are, 0 to 100.
Photo tools: the thickness of the guide lines: 0 thin, 1 medium.
The GPU the last Vulkan GPU benchmark result (PlusGPUBenchmarkGBps) was measured on.

The last Vulkan GPU benchmark result in GB/sec, raw (before PlusGPUBenchmarkVulkanScale*; 0: none). A new one within 8 percent of it keeps the higher of the two, so the GPU class does not change from start to start.

NVIDIA: scales the Vulkan GPU benchmark result to what the GL benchmark measures on the same GPU, for the GPU class lines (RTX 2080: GL 201.0 / Vulkan 191 = 1.05, research/117 9.7). Not saved: the build sets it.
AMD, Intel and others: as PlusGPUBenchmarkVulkanScaleNVIDIA (1: none; not measured against GL yet). Not saved: the build sets it.

At start, at most once a day, read PlusUpdateCheckURL and tell when a newer Charis Viewer is out: a band at the bottom of the login screen at every start while it is newer (research/325), or a small window when the answer comes once the login has started. Only a plain GET of that file is sent; like any web page, the site's log keeps the IP address and the viewer's version. On by default; Preferences > Setup and the band's "Stop notices" turn it off (then nothing is read or shown).

The update file the check reads (JSON, research/123). https only; http only to this computer (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]) to test with a local server. Redirects are not followed, so not a GitHub Releases download (a redirect) but the file on the repository's branch (research/123 5a). The default is the latest.json of noriaji/charis-viewer; empty: nothing is checked, even with PlusUpdateCheck on.
The version the user asked not to hear about ("Skip This Version"), e.g. 0.1.0-alpha.2+262911132. Empty: none.
When the update check last got an answer and judged it (seconds since 1970, UTC). Set to 0 to check again at the next start.

When the update check last started to read the file (seconds since 1970, UTC), kept before reading: a try without an answer is repeated an hour later at the earliest, even when the viewer ended while reading. Cleared to 0 when an answer comes.

Hosts whose pages the update band and window may open (download_url, notes_url), separated by commas. The default github.com is where the releases are (the update file itself is on raw.githubusercontent.com). Empty: only the host of PlusUpdateCheckURL. An address on any other host is left out.

The newer version the last answer of the update check named (its fields as in the update file, JSON), so the login screen tells of it at every start, also between the checks (research/325 4.2). It came from the server: every start reads it again as an answer (at most 16 KiB, the addresses and their hosts checked) and drops it when it is broken or no longer newer. Empty: none.

For the viewer installed with Setup.exe (Velopack; research/326): what is done when the update check (PlusUpdateCheck) finds a newer version. 0: only tell (the button opens the download page, as for the zip). 1 (default): ask; nothing is downloaded until the user presses Download. 2: download it without asking. In every case the new version is put in only when the viewer ends or with Restart and update; 0, or PlusUpdateCheck off, stops a download and throws a downloaded update away. Other values count as 1. No effect for the zip.

For tests, not saved: where updates cannot be installed (the zip, a viewer run from the build folder), a pretend update for the band, the window and the chip at the bottom right (research/326 section 5). 1: about 20 s for 280 MB, then ready ("Restart and update" does not quit). 2: fails at 40%. Nothing is sent or written. 0 (default): off. No effect where Setup.exe installed the viewer.

After login, until the agent's avatar is done (at most 120 s after the world shows): its bakes, attachment textures and meshes are fetched before the world's, and the world's requests in flight are held to 40% of the usual limit (slowed, not stopped). From the next login; turning it off ends it at once.

Textures on screen load first: those of near faces in view, then the rest in view, and well after them those that went off screen. A face counts as in view while it touches the view (with a small margin) and for a while after it left (30 s; shorter while video memory is short). Off: textures load by their size on screen alone, as before. LLRHI_TEX_VIEW_FETCH=0 keeps the fetch order as before whatever this says.

With PlusTexFetchRetry: how many times a texture that has no image yet and is refused with HTTP 403 (or another 4xx but 404, 410 and 429) is asked for again: 1 (default), 5 seconds after the failure on screen; 0: not at all (marked missing at once, as the official viewer); up to 4. In a live log all 74 refused textures were refused again on every try. A busy server (429, 5xx) and lost connections keep their own tries.

A texture whose download failed for a reason that may pass (HTTP 403 and the other errors but 404 and 410, a busy server, a lost connection) is asked for again, on screen first and after a wait that grows with every try (a 403 after 5 s, a busy server after 10 to 60 s), instead of staying grey for the whole session. Off: such a texture is marked missing at the first failure, as in the official viewer. LLRHI_TEX_FETCH_RETRY=0 also turns it off.

With PlusTexViewPriority: the coarsest level a texture on screen may stay at. 4 (default) or 3: it fetches more than the first 600 bytes for what is small on screen (about 50 KB for a 1024 pixel picture instead of 600 bytes; with VRAM about 24 KB more per picture), so it shows its colours instead of a nearly grey picture. 0 or 5 and up: off (as before: the first 600 bytes may be all); 1 and 2 count as 3. It gives way to the VRAM budget (the last resort from a divisor of 2, or a texture bias that is up for another reason than VRAM) and to the pressure stages for what has not been seen for a while. LLRHI_TEX_ONSCREEN_COARSEST=0 also turns it off.

With PlusTexViewPriority: a texture with no image yet whose faces are within the draw distance asks for at least this size on screen (pixels across, 0 to 64), so far and small things get their first coloured level instead of staying grey. 0: no floor (as before).

Texture and mesh downloads: the number of HTTP connections starts at 24 and follows the line, between 24 and 192. Every few seconds it goes up while all connections are busy and the server answers as fast as ever, a quarter down when the time to the first byte doubles, and half down when the server answers 429 or 503 (never below 24). Off: the limits stay fixed: textures at 24 (this viewer's default; the official viewer has 8), mesh at Mesh2MaxConcurrentRequests (8 unless you change it). Your own TextureFetchConcurrency / Mesh2MaxConcurrentRequests (up to 192) is used as it is and not tuned.

Shut down media plugins (SLPlugin and its browser helpers, about 0.6 GB each) that nobody uses: in-world media not drawn and out of earshot (PlusMediaReapDistance) for PlusMediaReapSeconds (PlusMediaReapTeleportSeconds after a teleport or a region change), and web browsers of the UI whose window is closed for PlusMediaReapUISeconds (not judged in mouselook, with the UI hidden, or in the photo screen). While more plugins run than PluginInstancesTotal, after 3 seconds. Never media with focus, the parcel media, HUD media, media loaded again less than 10 seconds ago, or while the window is minimized. Shown again, the media loads again (the page reloads). Off: the official behaviour (hidden media keeps its plugin).
PlusMediaReap: seconds in-world media is not drawn (and far away) before its plugin is shut down (2 to 3600).

PlusMediaReap: in-world media at least this many meters from both the avatar and the ear (the camera, or the avatar: MediaSoundsEarLocation) may be shut down (0 to 1024). Never less than MediaRollOffMax (where media sound fades out, 80 m by default), so media you can still hear keeps playing.
PlusMediaReap: after a teleport or a region change, seconds before far, undrawn media left behind is shut down (2 to PlusMediaReapSeconds).
PlusMediaReap: seconds a web browser of the UI (search, marketplace, destinations, web pages) stays loaded after its window is closed or hidden (2 to 3600). The login loads four of them hidden.

Diagnostics only (off by default). After login, log (tag SelfFirst) what the agent's cloud waits for: outfit and bake ids from the servers, the bakes' download, the attachments from the simulator, their meshes and textures, and the fetch queues meanwhile. Set it on the login screen (Debug Settings) before logging in; not kept between starts.

On: the statistics sent to the region at logout and quit (as every viewer sends) include the settings you changed: only on/off, number and color settings, never text or other free-form ones (login names, places, devices, paths, URLs), nor secrets (names with key, token, secret, password or api), nor the Charis settings (also the ones Charis added to the official settings.xml, and the Charis tone maps of RenderTonemapType). Off: no settings are sent with the statistics. Preferences > Privacy.
Where to report Charis bugs and ask questions, opened by Help > Report Bug. Empty: there is none yet; the menu item is hidden. Linden Lab's ReportBugURL is never used.
The Charis release notes page linked from About (and opened at start-up after an update on non-test channels). Empty: no link. Linden Lab's release notes pages are never used.
The downloadable build has turned a saved QAMode off once (it may have been saved by a developer build); after that QAMode is left to the user.

Mirrors (RenderMirrors) always show avatars and particles. Officially a mirror shows them only when its maker marked the reflection probe dynamic. Each mirror face then also draws the avatars in it (with the default RenderHeroProbeUpdateRate, three faces a frame). Off by default.

Your avatar mirrored in the floor it stands on or the water under it, on glossy floors and water (a planar reflection drawn before the main view from your eye mirrored in the plane; your avatar only, other avatars are not in it). 0 off, 1 the floor only, 2 the water only, 3 both (the higher plane under you). Not in first person or under water. Turning it on or off rebuilds the shaders. Needs reflection probes. Vulkan only.
The avatar reflection's picture size, a share of the screen's each way (0.25 to 1; 0.5 is a quarter of the pixels).

Debug: meters added to the height of the floor plane the server sends for your avatar (its collision plane) before your avatar is mirrored in it. -0.05 as the official viewer assumes for the ground under it. Change it if the reflection's feet do not meet yours.

The water as a mirror, as before PBR: the world drawn again from the camera mirrored in the region's water, read by the water in place of the reflection probes (the waves ripple it). 0 off, 1 the sky and the terrain, 2 also the trees and the grass, 3 also the objects, 4 also the avatars and the particles. Not while the camera is under the water or no water is in sight. Turning it on or off rebuilds the shaders (1 to 4 among themselves do not). Needs reflection probes. Vulkan only.

The water mirror's picture size, a share of the screen's each way (0.5 to 2; 0.5 is a quarter of the pixels, 2 four times as many, read back down to the screen's: supersampling). Larger is sharper and smoother at the edges but costs GPU time and VRAM in proportion to the pixels (2x is 16 times the default's); neither side goes beyond 4096. Changing it makes the mirror's targets again (no shader rebuild).

The water mirror is drawn every this many frames (1 to 4; 2 halves its cost). In between the last picture stays in place while the view turns; it is drawn at once when the camera moves a meter or turns about 10 degrees.

How far (m) the water mirror draws the trees, the grass, the objects and the avatars (16 up to the draw distance). The terrain and the sky have no limit. Past it the screen space reflections may still show what is on screen.
The sun's shadows in the water mirror (two cascades drawn again for the mirrored camera: more CPU, mostly with objects). Off: everything in the mirror is lit as if nothing cast a shadow.
How much the waves ripple the water mirror, times the water's reflection wavelet scale (0 a still mirror, 1 about as the water before PBR, up to 4).

Anti-aliasing of the water mirror, done where the water reads its picture (no pass or target of its own): 0 none (one bilinear read, as before), 1 edge smoothing as FXAA's (the steps along edges blended; a little more work on the water's pixels), 2 soft (four reads on a rotated grid: smoothest, slightly blurred). With PlusWaterMirrorScale above 1 every choice also averages the screen pixel's texels. No shader rebuild.

Development (speed, crowds): each avatar's bone matrices are handed to the Vulkan backend once a frame and every later pass (shadows, the main view, reflections) reuses that answer instead of asking again. The picture does not change. Environment LLRHI_SKIN_ONCE=1 turns it on and =0 off, whatever this says. With LLRHI_AVATAR_STATS=1, an "RHISkinOnce" log line every 5 s counts the reused and the asked rows.

Development: lets the test scene be built (plus/testscene: the MCP tools testscene_build/clear/stats, the LLRHI_CUE_DIR cue files testscene.build/testscene.clear, and "scene =" in a camerapath.run). A scene is a made-up load of objects that only this viewer has, above the avatar; nothing is sent to the simulator. Not saved: off at every start. Turning it off does not remove a scene already built (testscene_clear, a teleport or quitting do).

Screen space reflections in passes of their own, ported from Linden Lab's project/graphics-care-package: traced through a depth pyramid (longer reflections for the cost), blurred by the roughness, on surfaces up to RenderScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness (the official ones stop at 0.1). Needs RenderScreenSpaceReflections on; glass, alpha and water keep the official tracing. Vulkan only. On by default (and at every quality level but MidHigh, the one compared with the official viewer, and the GPU masks that cap it: Intel, Unknown, safe); it costs nothing while RenderScreenSpaceReflections is off (below High). Off: the official screen space reflections.

The water's screen space reflections (RenderScreenSpaceReflections, the official tracing) without the grain that comes while the camera moves: the same number of rays on a fixed ring instead of a random lean that changed every frame, no rays into the water and no hits on the water itself, hits faded near the screen's edge, and bright hits averaged down. The still picture stays about the same; no extra pass. Off: the official tracing on the water.

Hardware ray tracing for photos (research/230): only on a GPU that supports ray queries. Off by default and in no quality preset; nothing turns it on but this switch. Off costs nothing: no acceleration structure is built or kept.

Ray tracing for photos (PlusRayTracing): metres around the camera whose static opaque geometry goes into the acceleration structure. Larger takes more video memory and build time; things farther out do not appear in ray traced results.
Steps a screen space reflection ray takes through the depth pyramid at most (PlusSSR; GCP's RenderScreenSpaceReflectionIterations, which the official tracing still reads with its own meaning).

PlusSSR with RenderScreenSpaceReflectionTemporal: the share of the last frames' screen space reflections kept on avatars (0 to 1), whose skin and clothes move where the camera's motion does not take them. Lower: less trailing on shiny moving avatars, more noise on rough ones. 1: as the rest (and no avatar mark needed).

PlusSSR with RenderScreenSpaceReflectionTemporal: take the last frames' screen space reflections where the reflection was a frame ago (its mirror image, from the trace's hit distance) rather than where the surface was, clip them to the 5x5 neighbourhood's spread (PlusSSRClipSigma) and lean on the neighbours' rays where they were lost (not on mirrors, whose one ray is not noisy). Less grain on far reflections while the camera moves fast (research/294). 0: as before (the surface's motion, the 3x3's spread times 1.25), and no hit distance buffer.

For testing PlusSSRReflectionMotion: the half width of the box the last frames' screen space reflections are clipped to, in standard deviations of the 5x5 neighbourhood (0.5 to 4). Wider: less grain while moving, more trailing. Not saved.
PlusSSR (GCP's setting): how deep a surface is taken to be behind its depth, in meters; a ray passing further behind it goes on.
PlusSSR (GCP's setting): the ray's start pulled back along the surface normal, times the view depth (at least 1 cm).
PlusSSR (GCP's setting): no screen space reflections traced from or hit beyond this view depth (meters); they fade out over the last fifth.
PlusSSR (GCP's setting): no screen space reflections on rougher surfaces; they fade out over the last 0.1 below it.
PlusSSR (GCP's setting): the reflection buffer's size, a share of the screen's each way (0.25 to 1). 0.5 traces a quarter of the pixels.
PlusSSR (GCP's setting): a smaller reflection buffer is upsampled with the depth as the guide (no reflections bleeding across edges).

PlusSSR (GCP's setting): one screen space reflection ray a pixel each frame, added up over the frames with the camera's motion (cheaper, and smooth on rough surfaces while things hold still). Off: RenderScreenSpaceReflectionGlossySamples rays every frame. Snapshots always trace several rays.

PlusSSR (GCP's setting): the last frames' share of the screen space reflections with RenderScreenSpaceReflectionTemporal (0.5 to 0.98). Higher is smoother but trails more behind moving things; lower is sharper but noisier.
PlusSSR (GCP's setting): the spacing of the roughness blur's taps, in texels (0: no blur, rough surfaces reflect as sharp as polished ones).
Writes the navmesh data the simulator sends (Havok's format) to the log folder as navmesh_<direction>.bin, so that its format can be worked out. Off normally. Not saved: off again at the next start.

Screen effect preset drawn in the look pass (after the look's colors, for the screen and snapshots): film, polaroid, toy-camera, old-cinema, vhs or glow. Empty: the PlusFx sliders are used. Clarity and texture (PlusFxClarity, PlusFxTexture) are their sliders' either way; writing this setting (Debug Settings, an import) leaves them as they are. A UI that picks a preset, when one is made, is to go through plus::look::chooseFxPreset, which also writes the preset's values into them (research/275 L219). Vulkan only.
How strongly the screen effects are applied, 0 to 100 % (scales the preset or every slider).
Film grain, 0 to 100 % (used when PlusFxPreset is empty).
Darkened corners, 0 to 100 % (used when PlusFxPreset is empty).
Color fringes toward the edges, 0 to 100 % (used when PlusFxPreset is empty).
Red-orange glow round bright areas, 0 to 100 % (used when PlusFxPreset is empty).
Dust specks and scratches of old film, 0 to 100 % (used when PlusFxPreset is empty).
Video scanlines with a little wobble, 0 to 100 % (used when PlusFxPreset is empty).

Clarity: local contrast of larger areas (the brightness only, the midtones most), 0 to 100 % (research/249). Used with PlusFxPreset too: choosing a preset sets this to its value, moving it afterwards adds to the preset (research/275 L219).

Texture: local contrast of fine detail (stone, bark, leaves; the brightness only), 0 to 100 % (research/249). Used with PlusFxPreset too: choosing a preset sets this to its value, moving it afterwards adds to the preset (research/275 L219).
Soft glow: a wide blur of the whole picture laid back over it, so everything glows softly (research/286), 0 to 100 %. Used with PlusFxPreset too; scaled by PlusFxStrength.
How wide the soft glow's blur is, 0 to 100 % (about 0.6 % to 3 % of the picture's height). Only used when PlusFxSoftGlow is above 0.
How much light the soft glow adds on top of the blur (screen), 0 to 100 %: 0 is only a blur laid over the picture. Only used when PlusFxSoftGlow is above 0.
Draw the screen effects in snapshots only (their preview too); the screen stays clean.
Miniature (tilt-shift): a sharp band across the picture, a blur growing outside it, a little more color and contrast.
Miniature: where the sharp band's centre is, -1 (bottom of the picture) to 1 (top); 0 is the middle. Tilted, it moves across the band.
Miniature: the sharp band's height as a share of the picture's height (0 to 1).
Miniature: how strong the blur gets far from the band, 0 to 100 %.
Miniature: the band's slant in degrees, -90 to 90 (positive: anticlockwise).
Miniature: the saturation and contrast added, 0 to 100 %.
Subtitles: threads the recognizer uses (1 to 16). 4 keeps up with speech on a recent CPU; fewer is lighter but slower.
Subtitles: the language spoken, as a two letter code (en, ja, ...), or auto to find out for each sentence.
Subtitles: how many sentences the window keeps (1 to 100).
Subtitles: seconds the voice server's "is speaking" news arrives after the sound (can be negative). Used to find who spoke a sentence. Measure it with two people taking turns.
Subtitles: also translate each sentence with the translation service set in Preferences > Chat. The text of the sentence is sent to that service; off by default.
Subtitles: the language to translate into, as a code the service knows (ja, en, ...). Empty: the language chat translation uses.
Subtitles: cut sentences by who the voice server says is speaking, instead of by loudness. Takes effect when the window is opened.
Subtitles: also write out the parcel's internet radio, taken from the stream player's own sound (Windows 10 2004 or later), while nobody is speaking.

Subtitles: how sentences are translated. "service": the translation service set in Preferences > Chat (the text goes to it). "local": on this PC with models fetched from the window (research/217); nothing is sent anywhere.

Translation: write translations into Japanese in a dialect (as a game), for every translation (chat, IM, group chat, subtitles; local or service): "" standard, "kansai", "hakata", "tohoku". Only the translated text is changed, never what was said.
Translation: the folder (an https address) the local translation models are fetched from (en-ja.ctm, ja-en.ctm, m2m.ctm, ...). Empty: the address built in.
Area search: the columns of the list (bits: 1 distance, 2 name, 4 description, 8 price, 16 land impact, 32 prims, 64 owner, 128 group, 256 creator, 512 last owner).
Area search: the filter tab as saved by "Save as Default" (control name to value). Empty: the window's own defaults.
Area search: what a double click on a row does besides showing the object on the map (bits: 1 touch, 2 buy, 4 sit, 8 zoom the camera in).

Area search: list what avatars wear too (attachments and HUDs, yours and everyone's, with all their prims). Off: they are left out of the list and its counts; objects rezzed in world (animesh too) are listed either way.

Area search, while the window is open (metres, up to 512): (1) the list shows only objects within this distance of you; (2) the simulator is asked to send objects from this far, or from the draw distance when that is farther. 0: the draw distance (up to 512 as well), for both (1) and (2). What is drawn does not change; the farther objects are only listed.
