Radar: the columns of the list besides the name (bits: 1 same parcel/region, 2 sitting, 4 age, 8 payment info, 16 time seen, 32 range).
Radar: how names are written (0 display name, 1 user name, 2 display name (user name), 3 user name (display name)).
Radar: list only the avatars within PlusRadarRange.
Radar: the distance in meters that PlusRadarLimitRange limits the list to.
Radar: list the blocked avatars too (in italics).
Radar: say in the nearby chat when an avatar comes within chat range (20 m). With any of the six reports on, the radar works with its window closed.
Radar: say in the nearby chat when an avatar goes out of chat range.
Radar: say in the nearby chat when an avatar comes within the draw distance.
Radar: say in the nearby chat when an avatar goes out of the draw distance.
Radar: say in the nearby chat when an avatar comes into the region you are in.
Radar: say in the nearby chat when an avatar leaves the region you are in.
Local mesh: read a file again when it changes on disk (checked once a second), and show the new version on the objects showing it.
Local mesh: give the object the size the file has (in meters) when a mesh is shown on it; otherwise it keeps its own size. Attachments always keep theirs.
Protected folders: the UUIDs of inventory folders marked Protect. They cannot be deleted or moved elsewhere until unprotected (Firestorm: FSProtectedFolders).

Decode textures with slj2k, the Charis JPEG 2000 decoder (the same pixels as OpenJPEG, about 1.3 times faster per core; needs an AVX2 CPU). Images it cannot handle, and CPUs without AVX2, still use OpenJPEG. Off: OpenJPEG only.

Threads slj2k may use for one big image (1-8; 1: the decoding thread only). The image decode pool already runs several images at once, so 1 is usually right. Used for images of PlusJ2CDecoderThreadsMinArea pixels or more; OpenJPEG's own threading (the j2c-threads change) is not used for images slj2k decodes.
Decoded size in pixels (after the discard level) from which PlusJ2CDecoderThreads applies. 1048576 is 1024x1024.

Off by default. Keep a copy of what you wear, and where your modifiable attachments sit, in the account's folder (plus_outfit_backup.xml). At login, when the server comes back with an older outfit after a crash or a forced logout, offer to put the copy back. Whether the copy is kept is decided at login; turned off later, it stops at once.
Chat keyword alerts: a line of chat that holds a listed word gets a color, a sound and/or a notice (plus/keywords).
Keywords: look in IMs and group chat.
Keywords: the words, separated by a comma (, or the full width ， and 、).
Keywords: also look for your own names (display name, user name, first name).
Keywords: look in the speaker's name too.
Keywords: only whole words (a word written with spaces must stand alone; Japanese and Chinese words are found anywhere).
Keywords: ignore the differences of full width and half width characters and of hiragana and katakana.
Keywords: color the line of chat that holds a keyword.
Keywords: the color of such a line.
Keywords: play a sound when a line holds a keyword (not in Do not disturb).
Keywords: UUID of the sound (standard: the chat mention sound).
Keywords: show a notice on the screen when a line holds a keyword.

Inventory folder icons: each kind of system folder (Favorites, Outfits, Animations, Objects, Trash...) gets its own colour and emblem, and plain folders a plain manila folder (plus/invfoldericons). Off: the official icons.
Chat console: new nearby chat lines (also from people outside the screen) are shown at the bottom left of the screen, in the chat's colors, and fade out, while the nearby chat window is not open.
Chat console: seconds a line stays on the screen (the last two seconds it fades out).
Chat console: most lines shown at once.

Borderless fullscreen: the window has no frame and fills its monitor, without changing the display mode. Switched at once, no restart; off puts the window back where it was. Replaces the old exclusive FullScreen (a session that had FullScreen set starts borderless).
Preferences > Charis: the sub-tab shown when Preferences opens (display, graphics, controls, ai, rlva or other; another value: display). Written when a sub-tab is picked.
Shortcut bar: a row under the navigation bar with text-only buttons that run items of the menu bar. Add items with a right click on a menu item.
Shortcut bar: how dark the background under the buttons is (0 = clear, over the world as the Firestorm favorites bar; 1 = black).
Show UI button: with the UI hidden (Ctrl+Shift+U or Ctrl+Alt+F1), the mouse at the top edge of the window brings down a button that shows it again.

FPS display: the frame rate ("87 FPS", the median FPS, read every half second) is shown in the status bar right of the volume button, or in a corner of the screen under the windows (PlusFpsCornerPosition); never in a snapshot.

FPS display: where. 4 the status bar, right of the volume button (as Firestorm; not shown when the window is too narrow for it), or a corner of the screen: 0 top right, 1 top left, 2 bottom left, 3 bottom right (between the toolbars, under the menu and navigation bars and the notification icons).

Hitch log: when one frame lasts longer than this many milliseconds, the main thread's call stack is sampled every 100 ms and written to the log (group HitchLog) when the frame ends, or after 12 samples if it has not ended. 0 = off. For finding what freezes the viewer for a moment.

Exit time log: when the viewer closes, each stage of the exit (quit request, logout request and reply, each part of the cleanup, the Vulkan shutdown, the return from main) writes one line to the log (group Plus, lines starting with ExitTime [stage]) with the milliseconds since the quit began and since the previous line of the same side (the viewer's marks, or the Vulkan shutdown's own steps). Nothing runs while the viewer runs. Off: no clock and no log line (the setting is still read once when an exit begins). For measuring why closing is slow.

Exit watchdog (research/292): after the viewer has finished closing (settings and caches saved, "Goodbye!" logged), a small thread waits; if the process is still alive after PlusExitWatchdogSeconds, it writes the live threads and child processes to exit-watchdog.log (in the log folder) and ends the process. Also logs the thread and child process counts at the end of the exit (lines starting with ExitWatch). A normal exit never reaches the time-out; with a debugger or Tracy attached the report is written but the process is left alone. Off: nothing is started and nothing is logged (read once when the cleanup begins).
Seconds the exit watchdog waits after the viewer has finished closing before it ends the process (3 to 120). See PlusExitWatchdog.

While the viewer window has lost focus (you work in another window) but can still be seen (not minimized, not hidden, not on another virtual desktop, the computer not locked, no screen saver, no remote desktop disconnected), it keeps working as when it is in front: no sleep every frame, textures are not lowered after a minute, media keeps its priority. The frame rate is then the frame rate limit's and VSync's. A window that other programs' windows cover completely is not counted as seen here (one only partly covered still is): with PlusBackgroundHiddenStop (on by default) it sleeps and its media goes low priority, as in the official viewer, but its textures are kept (not lowered after a minute). Turn it off to save power with the viewer beside your work (as the official viewer: it sleeps, and drops texture quality after TextureDiscardBackgroundedTime). A window that cannot be seen is always as the official viewer. Debug setting only for now.

With PlusBackgroundKeepVisible on: a viewer window without focus that other programs' windows cover completely (nine points of it, once a second, none on a window of the viewer) counts as covered: the viewer sleeps every frame and media gets low priority, as the official viewer does, and is back to full at once when the window shows again (within a second or two). Texture quality is not lowered by this (a covered window can still be seen through a window capture). Layered or click-through windows on top (overlays) never count as covering. Turn it off when you share or stream the viewer window while it is covered (window capture in OBS, Discord, Teams, Zoom): then a covered window keeps working as in front. Debug setting only for now.

Frame rate limit: the most frames per second the viewer makes; 0 = no limit. A value from 10 to 1000. It holds also when VSync is off; with VSync on, a limit above the monitor's refresh rate does nothing. Graphics > Advanced has a button that sets it to the monitor's refresh rate.

Rain (PlusRain) wets what it falls on: while it rains, everything open to the sky (the ground, roofs, walls, objects, avatars) looks wet through the wet look, whatever PlusWetLook says: darker, glossier, puddles filling on level ground (PlusWetPuddles); a drizzle a little, a downpour all over. It builds up over seconds and dries over a few minutes after the rain stops. Places under a roof stay dry. Costs the wet look's GPU time (about half a millisecond) while it rains and until things have dried. Vulkan only.
When the flycam goes on, a short how-to once a session (plus/flycammouse). Its "Do not show again" turns this off.
Looking around with the mouse in the flycam (keyboard and mouse). 0 off; 1 while the right button is held (a short click is still a right click); 2 all the time (hold Alt to get the cursor back).

Leaving the flycam of the keyboard and the mouse keeps the camera where it is, as the camera controls leave it (until Esc or the controls bring it back to the avatar). Off: the camera goes back behind the avatar. A 3D mouse's flycam and the mouselook are not changed.
How far the flycam turns for a move of the mouse, as a factor on the mouselook's (MouseSensitivity). 1 = the same as in mouselook.
How many times faster the flycam flies while Shift is held (1 to 20).

How fast the flycam's tilt keys (Q and E, flycam_roll_left and flycam_roll_right) tilt the camera, in degrees a second (1 to 90; 3 times with Shift). The tilt is PlusCameraRoll's; it turns without a limit (kept within +-180).
How gently the flycam's keys start and stop, in seconds (0 to 2; 0 is off). The camera takes about this long to reach full speed and to stop.

The factor on how fast the flycam flies on the keys (0.05 to 50). The mouse wheel sets it while the flycam is on (hold Shift, Ctrl or Alt for the zoom instead). Preferences' Cancel puts back what its slider or Restore Defaults changed, not what the wheel set (the slider has no control_name, research/275 L071).

How fast the 3D mouse's camera (flycam) moves and turns, as a factor on FlycamAxisScale0-5 (1 = as set there). The number keys 1-9 set it from PlusFlycamSensSteps while the flycam is on; 0 puts it back to 1. The zoom axis is not scaled.
The factors the number keys 1-9 give PlusFlycamSens while the flycam is on, nine numbers separated by spaces, slowest first (0.01 to 100). A missing or bad one keeps the default.

DGC (VK_EXT_device_generated_commands: the GPU writes the draw commands of the reflection probes' faces). 0 auto: on with an NVIDIA GPU only (the only GPUs it was checked on), 1 on with any GPU that has it (not checked on AMD or Intel: turn it off again if something goes wrong), 2 off. Without it the faces are drawn from the GPU list without generated commands. Takes effect at the next start. The environment variable LLRHI_GPU_DRIVEN_DGC (0/1, for development) wins over it. Vulkan only.

Starts in a row that ended with the GPU lost (the device lost) while DGC was in use by PlusGpuDrivenDGC (auto or on). At 2 PlusGpuDrivenDGC becomes 2 (off) and this 0 again. A start where DGC runs and that ends any other way breaks the row (0), and so does DGC that ran 10 minutes before the loss; also 0 when a DGC choice is picked in the menu. A failed submit (most often out of memory) is not counted; a start where DGC did not run leaves it as it was. Kept by the viewer: not to be set by hand.

Offer to bring the settings of another viewer on this computer over (the official viewer, Firestorm, another Charis Viewer, ...) at the login screen. Set at the first start of this install, cleared once the window was closed.

At start, look once at which program opens secondlife:// links from the browser and tell (once the world is up) when it is not this viewer. Reads the registry only: registering is done by the button in Preferences > Setup. Off by default.

Do not draw the objects standing on a parcel of another owner than the parcel you are on (a parcel of the same owner counts as the same land). For you only: nothing is sent and others see them as before. Avatars and what they wear stay; so do the object you sit on and what you have selected. Hidden objects give no light and are not clicked.

Do not draw the objects standing on another parcel than the one you are on, whoever owns it (the parcels as the property lines cut them). For you only: nothing is sent and others see them as before. Avatars and what they wear stay; so do the object you sit on and what you have selected. Hidden objects give no light and are not clicked. With PlusHideOtherLandObjects on as well, this one decides.
Chat read-aloud: speak the chat that arrives with the Windows speech synthesizer (plus/tts). Off until you switch it on.
Read-aloud: read what the avatars near you say.
Read-aloud: read your own chat too.
Read-aloud: read the notices of the system (money, teleport results, region messages).
Read-aloud: read who comes into and goes out of range (the radar's reports).
Read-aloud window: show the details (voices, speed, limits).
Read-aloud: name of the system voice to use for a man ('' = choose by language).
Read-aloud: name of the system voice to use for a woman ('' = choose by language).
Read-aloud: speed of the voice (1 = normal).
Read-aloud: read only avatars and objects within this distance in meters (0 = any).
Read-aloud: a line longer than this many characters is cut.
Read-aloud: how many lines may wait; older ones are dropped.
Read-aloud: stay silent (and drop what waits) while the viewer window is in the background.
Read-aloud: when the chat translation added a translation to a line, read only the translation.
Read-aloud: say the speaker's name before an IM or group line.
Read-aloud: avatars whose voice you set by hand, as 'uuid:m;' (man) or 'uuid:f;' (woman). Written by the window and the avatar menu.

Ground fog drawn by the viewer (not the region's sky): 0 off, 1 light haze, 2 morning mist, 3 thick fog. Thickest at the ground and thinner with height (PlusGroundFogHeight); it glows toward the sun (PlusGroundFogGlow). Vulkan only.
Ground fog (PlusGroundFog): how high it reaches, in meters (the fog thins by a factor of e every this many meters above the ground).
Ground fog (PlusGroundFog): how much of the sun's light the fog scatters, 0 none (a gray fog), 1 normal, up to 4. Brightest looking toward the sun.

Fireflies drawn by the viewer: 0 off, 1 a few, 2 some, 3 many. Points of light that drift and blink in the air above the ground, fixed in the world, up to 40 m from the camera. Added before the glare, so bright ones get stars with the cross filter. Vulkan only; needs HDR (RenderHDREnabled).
Fireflies (PlusFireflies): their color, 0 yellow-green, 1 warm white, 2 gold, 3 blue.

Fireflies (PlusFireflies): how bright they shine, 1 normal, 0 invisible, up to 4. Under the "no post" tone mapping (a classic sky, or a sky with its reflection probe ambiance at 0) they are held just below white: above 1 they look as at 1.
Fireflies (PlusFireflies): how high above the ground they drift, in meters (they start 0.4 m above it).

Derez: an object deleted, taken or returned (anyone's) near you crumbles into glowing blocks that fly up instead of vanishing at once. Not avatars, attachments, rigged meshes, physical or moving objects, or the objects that go in a teleport or a region change. Your view only (nothing is sent).
Derez (PlusDerez): how long an object takes to crumble away, in seconds (0.4 to 4).
Derez (PlusDerez): objects farther from the camera than this (meters, up to 512) vanish as before.
Derez (PlusDerez): how many objects may crumble at once (0 to 64); more vanish as before.
Derez (PlusDerez): how many objects may start to crumble in one frame (0 to 64); more vanish as before.
Derez (PlusDerez): the colour of the glow: 0 cyan, 1 orange, 2 magenta, 3 green (as the materialize palette), 4 your own (PlusDerezColor).
Derez (PlusDerez): the glow's colour when PlusDerezPalette is 4 (sRGB, 0 to 1). Its brightness does not count: it is shown at the glow's full strength.
Time converter: the place of the third row ("pc" the clock of this PC, a name such as "jst" or "et", "u540" for UTC+9).
Time converter: the place of the fourth row (same ids as PlusTimeConvZone2).
Time converter: rows shown, 3 (SL time, UTC, a place) or 4 (two places).
Time converter: follow the clock (the rows move with the time; editing a field turns it off).

Temporal anti-aliasing (research/185): the last frame's picture is brought to this frame by the camera's motion and mixed in, after FXAA/SMAA (RenderFSAAType). With PlusTAAJitter the scene is drawn moved by a fraction of a pixel each frame, so thin edges and lines are smoothed over the frames. Things that move on their own (avatars, spinning prims) are only held back by the colours around each pixel. Snapshots and the probes' and mirrors' views are left alone. Vulkan only. Off by default; the quality levels set it (featuretable.txt): off at every level (2026-11-09: the avatar picture breaks up when it moves fast).
Temporal anti-aliasing: the share of the last frame's picture kept where the picture is still, 0.5 to 0.98 (less where it moves). More is smoother and slower to clear a trail behind a moving thing.

Temporal anti-aliasing's jitter (research/185 section 13): while PlusTAA draws, the main view's scene is drawn with the projection moved by a fraction of a pixel, a different one each frame (8 points), and TAA gathers them, so jagged thin edges and lines are smoothed where the picture is still. The cull, the shadows, the HUD and the UI are not moved; snapshots never are. Nothing changes while PlusTAA is off. On by default.
Temporal anti-aliasing's jitter: its size, 0 to 1 (1: the samples spread over the whole pixel; less: a smaller spread, sharper and less smooth; 0: none).

Temporal anti-aliasing (research/246, 250): how much of the history is kept, 0 to 1, where a thing finer than a pixel flickers with the jitter (a gap between the bars of a fence or the slats of a blind, a thin bar, a lattice seen at a slant, two faces in one plane): in some frames the jitter shows the whole neighbourhood one side of it only, and the history was cut to that side each frame. Only where the camera stands, the same surface stays nearest, the pixel's colour comes round with the jitter's round (8 frames), and that cut threw away 8 steps (of 255) or more in each of the last two rounds: a fine pattern that did not flicker is left as before. A thing that comes in front clears it at once, and a colour that turns against the round (the light changed, something went by at the same distance) within a frame or a few; a change of the light that keeps the pattern comes in over some frames on what is kept (a slow change lags most). A light blinking in step with the frames (every 1, 2 or 4 frames) is evened out while the camera stands, on a plain surface too. 1 (the default) stops the flicker; 0 keeps nothing (the other TAA changes of research/246 stay).

Upscaling (research/165): the world drawn at PlusUpscaleScale of the window's size and brought to it, for more frames per second where the GPU sets the pace (not where the CPU does). 0 off (the default), 1 AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 (EASU, sharpened by RCAS), 2 a plain bilinear stretch (as RenderResolutionDivisor, to compare). The HUD, the name tags and the UI stay at the full size; snapshots, and the view in the photo mode (the photo screen, or the photo tools open and not minimized), always are. While on, the official CAS is replaced by RCAS and the anti-aliasing is at least FXAA. Vulkan only.
Upscaling: the share of the window's width and height the world is drawn at, 0.5 to 1 (0.77 quality, 0.67 balanced, 0.59 faster, 0.5 fastest; 1 none). Used while PlusUpscale is on.
Upscaling: how much RCAS sharpens the upscaled picture, 0 (not at all) to 1 (the strongest). A matter of taste.

How many cull threads the viewer starts besides the main thread (they walk the octrees, sort the shadow casters and more, fork and join): 1 to 4, at most the CPU's cores less one; 0 (default) the cores less one, up to 3. From the next start.

Inventory window: show the detail pane (name, type, creator, owner, permissions, UUID of the selected item) on the right while the window is wide enough (PlusInvExplorerMinWidth). Turned on and off by the button at the right end of the search row, which shows while the window is wide enough; kept for the next session. Off, the pane is not updated and its width goes to the column on its left.

Inventory window: the width in pixels from which the detail pane shows (between the tab row and the received items, right of the tab's contents). It hides 40 pixels below it. Raised to what the folder tree's 240 and the detail pane's 200 minimums need.

Inventory window: the width in pixels of the detail pane, as last set by dragging the split before it (written when the split is let go or the window closes). Kept between 200 and 8192. A window too narrow for it shows the pane narrower (the center column gives way first, then the detail pane, then the folder tree) and keeps this width; the widths from which the detail pane and the three columns show count the pane at 200.

Inventory window: while the window is wide enough (PlusInvExplorerColumnsWidth), show three columns like a file explorer: the tab's folders on the left, the objects in the folder chosen there in the middle (through the tab's search and filter), the detail pane on the right. Off: one column as before.

Inventory window: the width in pixels from which the three columns show (PlusInvExplorerColumns). They go back to one column 40 pixels below it. Kept between 663 and 8192, and raised to what the left tree's 160, the center's 240 and (while it shows) the detail pane's 200 minimums need; a detail pane widened by hand does not raise it (it shows narrower).

Inventory window, three columns (PlusInvExplorerColumns): the width in pixels of the folder tree on the left, as last set by dragging the split between it and the center column (written when the split is let go or the window closes). Kept between 160 and 8192; a narrow window gives the center column its 240 and the detail pane its 200 first. A wider window widens the center column only.
Inventory window: the custom filter tabs made with "+" (an array of maps with 'name', 'filter', 'states' and 'tabhidden' keys). Kept per account.
Enables the experimental fix for attachments getting detached on teleports and region crossings.
Delay in seconds after a teleport for that kill object messages to detach attachments are being ignored.
If enabled, reports attachments that were attempted to get detached during a teleport or region crossing to nearby chat.
Show the particle cloud around an avatar that is still loading. Off: nothing is drawn for it until it is loaded (the official viewer shows the cloud).

Draw your own avatar while it is still loading (from the login on) as a wireframe, and any avatar whose body textures (bakes) are not loaded yet as a wireframe too. Needs RenderGrayTextureWireframe. Off: your own avatar is not drawn until it is loaded (as the official viewer).

With TAA (research/289): its jitter is held still while the wireframes of textures not loaded yet (and the lines of a materialize band) cover enough of the view, near ones (lines thinner than a pixel came and went with it), not for every far one (a busy venue short of VRAM held it nearly all the time). Needs RenderGrayTextureWireframe. Off: held while any wireframe is drawn (as before).

Materialize (research/256): the wireframe of an object whose texture is still loading glows in the colour of PlusMaterializePalette, and when the texture comes, a band of light sweeps the object from the bottom up, turning the wireframe into the real surface. Not alpha; avatars with PlusMaterializeAvatar; what comes at once from the cache shows at once. Needs RenderGrayTextureWireframe. Off: the plain cyan wireframe, and the texture shows at once.

Materialize avatars too (research/259, with PlusMaterialize): an avatar drawn as a wireframe while it loads (your own from the login on, PlusAvatarWireframeLoading; anyone whose body or attachment textures are not loaded yet) is swept once by a band of light from its feet to its head when it has them all, turning the wireframe into the real body, clothes and attachments. At most 8 avatars at once (more show at once). Avatars never shown as a wireframe show at once. Off: the wireframe turns into the avatar at once.
Materialize: how long the band of light takes from the bottom of a surface to its top, in seconds (0.4 - 4).
Materialize: the colour of the wireframe and the band. 0 cyan, 1 orange, 2 magenta, 3 green, 4 PlusMaterializeColor.
Materialize: the colour of the wireframe and the band while PlusMaterializePalette is 4 (red, green, blue, 0 - 1).

Materialize, for debugging (research/278): every 5 s, a line in the log (tag Materialize) of what the bands did since the line before: why the textures that came took no band or that they took one (came: each call of GrayWire::onImageCreated; one drawn only in the shadow, reflection and probe passes has no wait, unwaited; one whose band waited for its alpha analysis, mask wait, is counted there when its band starts, not at all when it never does), the same for the avatars that stopped being a wireframe (avatar), and the draws of batches whose band was under way (drawn: sweep, flash, flat, worn, body, no_program, none, alpha), the batches that took none by render pass; research/289: the draws of batches not drawn as a wireframe with a texture drawn as the gray stand-in for good (gray: given_up, its wait given up while it is fetched; given_up_idle, while nothing fetches it; missing, its asset missing), by render pass too, and the failed tries to make an image, VRAM short and the like (not draws: gray image_failed, of a texture given its pixels, each try; target_failed, of render targets and other images; only failures of ensure_image when it creates an image, not rebuilds that keep the original image); the groups built again for an alpha mask under a second after their last build (mask again). No line while nothing happened. Off: nothing is counted. Not saved (as the other diagnostic logs): to count a login, turn it on at the login screen or start with --set PlusMaterializeLog 1.

For debugging (research/284): when the alpha analysis of a texture that came (done on another thread for one of 64 pixels or more) tells otherwise than its faces were built with, their groups are built again, so that a texture whose alpha is a cut-out (leaves, grass, fences, signs) goes to the alpha mask pool (faster, drawn by the materialize band) instead of staying in the alpha blend pool; a texture analysed before keeps its mask while it is analysed again at a new resolution; a materialize band waits for the analysis (at most 0.5 s, a wireframe meanwhile), and an alpha blended surface stays a wireframe while its texture's band sweeps (one about to be built again for the mask pool does not show ahead of the band). Works with or without PlusMaterialize. PlusMaterializeLog counts it (mask). Off: as upstream (no mask until the analysis comes, nothing built again, an alpha blended surface shows at once). Not saved.

If enabled, the mouse wheel over a closed drop-down changes its selection (the official behaviour). Off by default: the wheel goes on to the panel behind it, so scrolling a panel does not change a setting by mistake.

Login: the curtain lifts once the agent's avatar is there and 97% of the region's land has come (at least 1 s after the world began to draw under it, at the latest after PrecachingDelay), without waiting for the clothes (they go on loading in the world), and fades in 0.7 s; a first login keeps these official waits. Also (a first login too): the image decoding before the simulator's circuit takes 0.2 s (official 2 s), a finished startup state goes on to the next one in the same frame, and the progress screen is presented from inside the startup states at most 30 times a second. Off: all the official waits (6 s, then the clothes up to 10 s, a 1 s fade, 2 s of decoding, one state per frame).

With PlusFastLogin: the simulator's circuit (UseCircuitCode) is asked as the wait for the seed capability begins, so the two overlap (official: after the seed's answer and the decoding). The circuit is then not read until the login reaches the world wait; the login timeline logs how long. Off by default until it has been tried on Second Life and OpenSim grids.

Teleport: the curtain lifts once 97% of the new region's land has come (at least 0.4 s after the arrival, at the latest after TeleportArrivalDelay), and after an arrival the far range asked of the simulator comes back from its half in half steps instead of tenths (other raises of the draw distance, and memory coming back, keep the tenths). Off: the official 2 s and tenths.

Teleport: the dark teleport screen (the progress view) does not come down; the world stays in view while the teleport runs (Firestorm's FSDisableTeleportScreens). Not the login's or the logout's screen. Off: the official screen.

Log only: one line per login (tag LoginTimeline, "login timeline") with each startup state's time since the login began, until the curtain has gone, and one line per teleport ("teleport timeline"). Whether PlusFastLogin and PlusFastTeleport are on or off, so the two can be compared.

Teleport back to a region you just left: its textures stay sharp. The viewer already keeps a region you leave, with all its objects, until the simulator closes it (about 50 s); after a teleport the old region's textures are normally lowered at once so the new region has room in video memory. With this on, the textures of the last few regions you visited (PlusRegionParkMax) are left as they are while video memory has room (under 80 % of the budget, no texture pressure, no discard bias, system memory not short), and stay in memory PlusRegionParkTextureHold seconds after the region closes (30 s otherwise). When video memory runs short they are lowered as before. Off: as before.
With PlusRegionPark: how many of the regions visited before this one keep their textures (1 to 8). A visit runs from a teleport or the login to the next teleport.
With PlusRegionPark: seconds a parked region's textures stay in memory once nothing uses them (its region has closed), while video memory has room (30 to 600; 30 s otherwise).

After a teleport or the login, the objects the object cache already has are made as soon as they arrive, within the draw distance and large enough on screen, also those behind the camera (otherwise only those in view, the rest when you turn). For 30 s after the arrival, PlusRegionParkEagerPerFrame a frame (twice that while the teleport screen is up); not while video memory or system memory runs short, nor on a walking region crossing. Off: as before.

With PlusRegionParkEager: cached objects out of view queued for creation a frame, a linkset counted with all its parts (1 to 2048; twice that while the teleport screen is up; at most 2048 cache entries are looked at a frame). Higher fills the scene sooner, with longer frames.

After a teleport to another region, a line in the log (tag TPLag) at the arrival and 1, 3, 10, 30, 60, 120, 180 and 300 s after it: the frame time since the line before, video memory against the driver's budget with the Vulkan blocks and pools, vertex buffers, textures, discard bias and texture pressure, the regions still open with their objects, and what the GL buffer compaction gave back (research/245). Also, once the discard bias has stayed over 1.5 for 20 s (a teleport or not), a line (tag BiasWatch) every minute until it has been back at 1 for 30 s: how the bias went up and down, what the memory guard saw, the viewer's memory (research/309). Nothing else runs between teleports.

Gives back the room left inside video memory blocks, so the half-empty blocks a teleport or a crowded event leaves go back to the driver instead of keeping video memory over its budget (very slow frames and blurry, gray textures for minutes). It starts when video memory in use reaches 92% of the driver's budget, or earlier while textures are held blurry for lack of video memory (128 MB under the use where they come back sharp), and once started goes on until the use is 64 MB under where it started; while textures are held blurry, until it is under 85% of the budget or 64 MB under that start, whichever is lower. It also stops once neither part finds anything more to give back. For a few frames after it gave blocks back, no empty block is kept. The GPU copies of the vertex and index buffers in the emptiest blocks are given back (each buffer keeps its copy in system memory and gets a GPU copy again when next drawn, at most 64 MB of them a frame), and the textures of the texture blocks at most half in use are copied on the GPU into fuller blocks (at most 48 MB a check). Nothing happens while video memory has room. On by default since research/285. Off: the blocks stay until they empty. LLRHI_VK_BUFFER_COMPACT=0 keeps the buffers' part off, LLRHI_TEX_COMPACT=0 the textures' part, LLRHI_VK_EMPTY_TRIM=0 keeps the empty blocks.

With PlusBufferCompact: seconds a buffer was not drawn before it no longer counts as in use when its memory block is weighed (0 to 60). A block whose buffers in use take at most half of it gives back the GPU copies of all its buffers: those drawn lately get one again at once in a fuller block, the others when next drawn. 0: every buffer counts as in use, so only blocks at most half full are emptied.

With a GPU that has no video memory of its own (integrated), or a line set in PlusMemGuardFreeMB: while the PC has less free memory than the line, the textures go down (the texture budget reacts as to low memory, or, with PlusMemGuardSoftOnly, as to a short video memory while only what is off screen goes down; they come back, slowly, once the PC has had for 10 s the line and half of it more free, at least 512 MB more but at most 1 GB more), and large texture decodes wait, one passing every quarter second; they also wait, one every 2 s, while more than 256 MB of decoded textures wait for the main thread. A texture's first small image, local files and bakes never wait. Nothing changes otherwise. Off, or a discrete GPU with no line set: only the official reaction under RenderMinFreeMainMemoryThreshold.

With PlusMemGuard's line: when the PC's free memory is under the line but not under the emergency line (the larger of 512 MB and a third of the line), only what is off screen goes down and large decodes wait a little (one every 100 ms); what is on screen stays as sharp as it is. Only when the free memory falls under the emergency line does the guard act as before (what is on screen goes down too). A dip under the line that lasts under 3 s raises nothing (large decodes already wait), the pass over every texture runs at most every 10 s when the guard alone starts it, and the textures come back 10 s after the free memory has been over the low end of the line (60 s before), a Soft-only raise at up to three times the base speed (at most 0.3 a second). It needs the view split of PlusTexViewPriority (off, or in the safe start: the guard is as before). Off: the guard as before (the line alone is an emergency).

The memory guard's line (PlusMemGuard), MB of free memory (256 to half the PC's memory). 0: automatic, a sixteenth of the PC's memory (768 MB to 2 GB) with a GPU that has no video memory of its own (integrated), none with a discrete one.
